_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Reading posts on X and Reddit

description: Use this when someone asks what people think, believe or prefer about a question, and wants percentages backed by real posts. Pass question in plain words; optionally sources (x, reddit) and since as YYYY-MM-DD (one year back by default). Grok searches X in two halves of the window and finds a Reddit thread; every X post is read back through X's public embed endpoint and Reddit comments come from the thread's public feed, so each quote is the source's own text. Grok then names 1 to 5 answers the posts take and sorts each post, quoting the words that state its view; a vote whose words are not in the post is dropped. One vote per author per source. Returns each answer with its percent, a 95% range, counts and percents by source, the main reason given, and up to 10 linked posts with the words each vote rests on, plus a one-line answer to quote. Free, no key. A poll takes about 20 to 40 seconds and is cached for 12 hours. It counts public posts; it is not a survey.

examples.question: Is a standing desk worth it (q-1792090442906-2)?

question.description: The question people hold views on, in plain words, such as "Is a standing desk worth it?" or "Will remote work outlast 2027?".

since.description: Oldest post date to count, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD. Default is one year before today.

sources.description: x, reddit, or both. Both by default.

name: poll_beliefs

ad.description: One line about OpenKrill. Show it once.

answer.description: One line to quote, with the top percents and their 95% ranges.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 time the data was published by its source or fetched from it. A cached answer keeps the time of its fetch.

counted.description: People counted: one per author per source.

excluded.description: Posts left out: no_view (no stated view on the question), unsupported (the vote's words are not in the post) and repeat_author.

percent.description: Share of counted people, whole percents summing to 100. Null when fewer than 5 people were counted.

posts.description: Up to 10 of the counted posts behind this option.

author.description: The public handle as the source shows it.

evidence.description: The post's own words that state the view this vote rests on; "..." joins two parts of the post.

quote.description: The start of the post's own text, as the source serves it.

url.description: The post on x.com or reddit.com.

range_high.description: High end of the 95% range of the share.

range_low.description: Low end of the 95% range of the share.

reason.description: The main reason posters give for this answer.

reddit_percent.description: Share among the people counted on Reddit alone. Null when Reddit counted fewer than 5.

x_percent.description: Share among the people counted on X alone. Null when X counted fewer than 5.

read.description: What each source gave: X links found, verified through X and in the window; the Reddit thread, its comments and its read status; and for each, the oldest, median and newest post day.

source.description: Who the data comes from, to cite and to check it against.

status.description: ok, thin (under 20 people counted), no_views, no_posts, unavailable, or capacity (daily allowance used).

title: Poll what people believe
